prompts.baseline:
Describe only the house's architecture in the supplied schema.
Image 1 establishes the FRONT and the single left-to-right 0..1 facade axis.
Other images show the SAME house: use them to resolve roof planes, depth and garage
entry, never transfer their image coordinates or side-facing features to the front.
Volumes are non-overlapping FRONT rectangular wall regions up to their eaves.
Count full wall stories below the eaves, NOT windows or attic triangles. Separate
one-story wings from a narrower two-story centre when the eave heights differ.
Each volume has an underlying roof: parallel is across the house front;
perpendicular is front-to-back. Read the roof planes behind visible triangles.
A front triangle can be a cross-gable on a parallel ridge or the end of a
perpendicular ridge. Porch gables belong to porches. Dormers belong to volumes.
Describe one continuous porch cover, including a small entrance gable separately.
Keep relative facade widths and forward/recessed wall relationships. An L-shaped
wing can have intersecting ridges: record its dominant underlying ridge and explain
the intersection in evidence/limitations. Do not invent another story to encode it.
Use unknown for unseen geometry. Garage side is house-front left/right; garage_entry
is front, side, or unknown. A hidden garage must not determine visible roof geometry.
IDs are unique; owners reference existing volumes or porches. Explain story and roof
decisions briefly in evidence, citing image numbers. No windows, doors, materials,
bounding boxes, renderer slots or configuration. Do not optimize for a particular style.

Before assigning roof directions, identify the FRONT wall plane from the main entry,
wall corners, and window rows. In an oblique photo the side wall is also visible:
a triangular end on that side is not a front-facing gable. Judge parallel versus
perpendicular relative to the physical front wall, not the image's horizontal axis.
Briefly identify the front plane and distinguish any visible side plane in evidence.
Do not allocate a front volume merely because a side wall is visible.

manifest.protocol: Assistant visual labels fixed before these model trials; not independently human-adjudicated. Labels never included in provider prompts. Existing brick case is development, remaining cases are evaluation references. Bungalow is a difficult oblique holdout: its roof partition is provisional and must be visually adjudicated, not treated as definitive ground truth.

cases.label_notes: Central small entry; right window awning is not a porch. Width tolerance .12; attic triangles are not full stories.
Two projecting wings, recessed middle. Small door canopy only; courtyard is open.
Two full front wall stories. Small entry porch roughly .2 of facade, no broad cover. Parapets/chimneys are unsupported; foliage obscures far left. Side wall is not another front region.

Mixed full wall stories; front runs from left-wing front corner to right-wing front end. Exclude left side-facing gable/porch. Strong perspective: .15 boundary tolerance. Ridge of partly obscured right wing less certain. Reinspection: entrance and rows of windows establish the long front wall; triangular masonry ends and chimney stacks are on the left SIDE. Far-right wing roof is excluded from scoring because foliage obscures it.

Held out from first comparison: one-story front-gable bungalow, attic opening is not a second wall story; recessed right porch covers roughly .35-.5. Strong perspective and foliage limit exact widths. Main gable continues behind porch; no separate full second story. Reinspection: one wall story and covered entry are visible; exact roof partition/front-plane extent is ambiguous. Roof and mass-count labels are provisional and excluded from automatic scoring.
